correctness.rationale: With E=exp((T/2)A_+), the monodromy is E^T E. Its normalized determinant is one, and half the trace of exp(dT)E^T E is half the squared Frobenius norm of exp((T/2)(A_++dI)), namely 1+2 cosh(h)^2 sinh(rT/2)^2. Its larger eigenvalue gives the stated Floquet exponent. For C=cosh(h)>1, g(z)=asinh(C sinh z) has g(0)=0 and g''(z)=C(1-C^2)sinh(z)/(1+C^2 sinh(z)^2)^(3/2)<0 for z>0. Thus g(z)/z strictly decreases from C to 1, yielding exactly the threshold regime, including persistence at d=r and extinction at d=rC for every finite T. If X=Phi(t)u(0), exact division by H=1+kappa times the integral of the total of X solves the nonlinear equation; positivity guarantees H>=1 globally. The positive monodromy gives X(nT+s)=Phi(s)[a mu^n v+O(nu^n)] with a>0 including for axis initial states and 0<nu<mu. For mu<1 the numerator gives uniform exponential decay. For mu>1 the Poincare map has the unique positive fixed point (mu-1)v/(kappa I) and summing the Perron geometric series in H proves phase-uniform attraction to the stated orbit. For mu=1 the complete periods contribute kappa a n I+O(1) to H and the partial period is uniformly bounded, while the numerator tends uniformly to a Phi(s)v. Multiplication by nT+s cancels a and gives the claimed strictly positive universal coefficient, confirming algebraic rather than exponential decay. The example matches the Gram-matrix eigenvalue and the threshold equation.
residual_risks: The numerical example is only corroboration; criticality and its phase-uniform limit use the exact critical parameter, not a finite precision root or finite-time simulation. Equal half-seasons, strict positivity of the parameters, and the common scalar quadratic brake matter to the result.

value.rationale: The transpose switch is a minimal explicit cooperative model where individually stable seasons can sustain persistence. Exact monotonicity determines when switching speed can reverse extinction and supplies a sharp unique boundary rather than a sufficient condition. At that boundary the positive phase profile gives the actual asymptotic abundance and composition independently of the initial population, distinguishing the critical regime from exponential extinction.
residual_risks: This is a mathematically specified shared-crowding model. The result does not establish thresholds under arbitrary unequal phases, crowding models, or empirical ecological systems.
